newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Owens Corning sees sales rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Owens Corning sees sales rise.

text.p: Owens Corning expects 1997 sales of about $4.1 billion and, in 1999, targets $5 billion, chief financial officer David Devonshire said Thursday. Owens Corning makes glass composites and building materials.
"We are looking at (1997) sales growth in the neighborhood of eight percent," he said in a telephone interview. "Our target is to record sales in the year 1999 of $5 billion."
As reported, 1996 sales were $3.83 billion, six percent higher than 1995's. Its $5.50 a share loss for 1996 reflects special charges such as $542 million for asbestos reserves.
Excluding charges, earnings from ongoing operations were $4.65 a share versus 1995's $4.25.

Fourth quarter net income of $1.25 a fully diluted share includes a pretax charge of $43 million for restructuring plus one-time tax benefits. Excluding special items, fourth quarter ongoing operating earnings were $1.24 a share versus $1.06.

The company stopped making asbestos years ago but lawsuits are pending. Devonshire said reserves are adequate to cover "any and all claims," including a Florida jury award this week of $31 million to a man due to cancer linked to asbestos.
Owens Corning expects the amount to be reduced under Florida tort law and is appealing the case, Devonshire said.
The stock was off 3/4 to 47-3/8 on the New York Exchange.
About $450 million of 1996 sales came from 12 acquisitions completed in the last 30 months, and in 1997 that number will be more than $500 million, Devonshire said.
The company will continue to seek acquisitions that fit with existing product lines and markets and add to earnings within the first full year after completion, he said.
In Europe, business has been hurt by a weak economy, but January orders are up there and the company expects an improved Europe second half, Devonshire said.
